text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Monday morning newspapers:
- The Defence Ministry has not yet found out the cause for Friday's explosion at an artillery training that killed one soldier and wounded two.

- The Christian Democratic Party has not yet publicly revealed its programme of changes that should improve the party's position after the number of its parliamentary seats fell to 10 from 15 at the November general election.
- The centre-right Social Democrats pushed for a common declaration of all parliamentary parties whereby they would express their full support for Slovenia joining NATO as soon as possible.
- The government has not yet prepared a law that would privatise Slovenian casinos.
- Bicycle maker Rog said improving productivity of its employees was the precondition towards overcoming financial problems that threaten bankrupting the company.
- The Chamber of Economy this year awarded 11 enterpreneurs for their business achievements.
- Export and import duties for trade with Romania will be greatly reduced from July 1 when Romania will become a member of the Central European Free Trade Agreement.
- Slovenia and Austria opened three additional common border crossings for European Union citizens. Until now the three crossings could only be used by Austrians and Slovenians.
